attractions.name: Umerkot Fort
attractions.description: A historic sandstone fort where Mughal Emperor Akbar was born in 1542, one of Sindh's most significant historical sites.

attractions.name: Thar Desert Gateway
attractions.description: Umerkot marks the entry point to the Thar Desert, with sand dunes and traditional desert villages nearby.

attractions.name: Shiv Mandir & Hindu Temples
attractions.description: Umerkot has a large Hindu community and several notable temples reflecting Sindh's religious diversity.

weather_info.climate_type: Hot, semi-arid to arid climate typical of interior Sindh
weather_info.avoid_months: May to July (extreme heat, often above 40°C)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild and pleasant, 10-24°C, best time to visit
Occasional heavy rain, humid, risk of flooding in low areas

travel_tips.tip: Visit Umerkot in the cooler months (November to February) for the most comfortable travel experience.
Intercity buses and shared vans (Suzuki/coaster) are the most common way to reach and travel around the district.
As with most small-town travel in Sindh, arrange accommodation and local guides in advance, especially outside the main town center.

history.founded: An ancient town on the edge of the Thar Desert, historically significant since at least the medieval Sindhi Soomra era
history.city_history: Umerkot is famously the birthplace of Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1542, born while his father Humayun was in exile there. The town has a significant Hindu population and sits at the gateway to the Thar Desert.
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
